$comment: Neutral shipped <sys/time.h> (POSIX) — SEED of the struct-body descriptor surface (the FIRST `structs` consumer). ★ c83 (D-FFI-MACHO-TIMEVAL-TV-USEC-WIDTH): `struct timeval` DIVERGES per format → per-format `variants` (the plan-25 mechanism sys/stat.json seeded). glibc LP64 (both elf arches, verified /usr/include/x86_64-linux-gnu/sys/time.h → bits/types.h: time_t AND suseconds_t are `long`) is {tv_sec i64 @0, tv_usec i64 @8} sizeof 16, no padding — ONE elf variant covers x86_64+arm64 (like flock's). Darwin keeps tv_sec `long` (xnu bsd/arm/_types.h + bsd/i386/_types.h: `typedef long __darwin_time_t`) but tv_usec is 32-BIT: xnu bsd/sys/_types.h `typedef __int32_t __darwin_suseconds_t`, and bsd/sys/_types/_timeval.h declares _STRUCT_TIMEVAL {__darwin_time_t tv_sec; __darwin_suseconds_t tv_usec;} → macho {tv_sec i64 @0, tv_usec i32 @8} = 12 payload + 4 TRAILING pad = sizeof 16 (the layout engine derives the pad from the 8-alignment). ★ THE SAME-SIZE TRAP (the c15c stat lesson): sizeof agrees at 16 on BOTH formats, so a size check cannot discriminate — a macho READ of tv_usec through an i64 field folds the 4 padding bytes into the high half (little-endian misread of undefined stack bytes) and a WRITE clobbers them; gettimeofday (sqlite os_unix reads tv_usec) + utimes consume the layout. Pins: RealSysTimeTimevalPerFormatLayout (tests/ffi — reads THIS file per format; red if the macho variant regresses to i64 or is dropped) + shipped_timeval_macho (the darwin-CI runtime witness). Field types are the RESOLVED hir-text form (parseTypeFromText resolves hir-text builtins, not descriptor typedef names). The semantic phase interns the struct + injects `timeval` into the TAG namespace + a field scope, so c `struct timeval tv; tv.tv_sec` resolves and the layout engine derives the offsets from the field sizes. A SUBDIRECTORY descriptor (sys/time.json — resolved by the c6 subdir fix, distinct from <time.h> → time.json). c51 added the first symbol utimes; c53 added gettimeofday(struct timeval*, void* tz). ⚠ THE CLAUSE THAT FOLLOWED WAS TRUE WHEN WRITTEN AND IS NOW HALF REFUTED, so it is restated rather than deleted: it read 'both ptr<void> (SQLite passes &tv + a 0/NULL tz, so struct timezone needs no shipped body; the surfaces are additive — struct timezone stays deferred until a use needs its body)'. ✔The `tz` half STANDS and is stronger than 'deferred': glibc's own <sys/time.h> spells that parameter `void *__restrict __tz` (verified in WSL, x86_64 AND the aarch64 cross headers) and the macOS SDK agrees, so `ptr<void>` there is the REFERENCE type, not a stand-in — struct timezone is not merely unshipped, it is not in the prototype at all. ✔The `tv` half was a DEFECT wearing the words 'per house style' — [[D-FFI-SHIPPED-DESCRIPTORS-DECLARE-STRUCTS-THEIR-OWN-SIGNATURES-DO-NOT-USE]], closed P56 lane sv — and is now `fn(ptr<timeval>, ptr<void>) -> i32`, one BY-NAME reference resolved AFTER variant selection, so the elf read binds {i64,i64} and the macho read {i64,i32} from ONE signature. That the two parameters end up spelled DIFFERENTLY is the whole point: this row now states which pointer carries a layout and which genuinely does not. ★ D-CSUBSET-DARWIN-BSD-SYMBOL-CLUSTER: futimes — SDK sys/time.h:192 `int futimes(int, const struct timeval *)`, libSystem export (link-verified); the timeval pointer keeps utimes' own spelling — ⚠ WHICH IS NO LONGER `ptr<void>`, and the parenthetical that justified it ('the SOLE consumer passes NULL, so no layout knowledge rides on the parameter') is restated rather than deleted because it argued from ONE CALL SITE to a TYPE, which is the wrong direction: a shipped signature states what the API IS, not what today's consumer happens to pass. Both are now `ptr<timeval>` (P56 lane sv), matching `int futimes(int, const struct timeval *)` in the SDK and glibc alike; a NULL still passes, because a null pointer constant converts to any pointer type. That consumer: sqlite os_unix.c:7883 `futimes(conchFile->h, NULL)` in proxyTakeConch, inside `#if defined(__APPLE__) && SQLITE_ENABLE_LOCKING_STYLE` — glibc also exports futimes but zero elf consumers exist → per-symbol [macho] by the no-over-ship rule (the fdatasync elf-only gate, mirrored). S0001 without the row; pinned by tests/ffi RealSysTimeJsonFutimesMachoOnly + the shipped_bsd_random_futimes_uuid_macho corpus (fd -1 → EBADF no-op, so the call crosses the ABI without touching any file). ★ D-CSUBSET-DARWIN-BSD-STRUCT-BY-NAME: `struct itimerval` (SDK sys/time.h:92) is the FIRST consumer of the BY-NAME composite field route — its two members spell `"type": "timeval"`, the bare TAG NAME of the entry ABOVE, which the structs loop now publishes into the descriptor's working name vocabulary exactly as the typedefs/unions loops already published theirs. So itimerval needs NO `variants` OF ITS OWN: the by-name reference resolves to whichever timeval variant this target selected, and the ONE place a tv_usec width is stated stays the timeval entry. MEASURED natively (arm64 Darwin, offsetof): sizeof(struct itimerval)==32, it_interval@0, it_value@16, _Alignof 8 — and glibc LP64 agrees at 32/0/16 even though its inner tv_usec is 8 bytes wide, which is precisely the divergence by-name absorbs for free (a restated body would have to get both right, twice). WHY IT MATTERS: a descriptor SHADOWS the real header text, so `struct itimerval` was simply MISSING from a TU that includes <sys/time.h> — and xnu sys/proc.h's `struct extern_proc` embeds one BY VALUE, so extern_proc had an incomplete member, stayed incomplete itself, and made kinfo_proc's kp_proc a second incomplete member: sqlite test1.c + mem1.c emitted 4 S0026 from that ONE hole. The reader SKIPS (never errors on) an entry whose by-name dependency is declared-but-unselected — on a pe/unknown-format read no timeval variant matches, so itimerval is simply absent there too, exactly as its dependency is. Pinned by tests/ffi RealSysTimeItimervalByNameComposite (size/offsets + FIELD-TYPE IDENTITY with the timeval entry, both formats).
